title: EDR_T3 TILT-NOW adjudication — verdict
method: least-squares plane fit z=ax+by+c on local-planar DEMs (NOT pixel-differencing); long=atan(a) cross=atan(b)

reference.fetched: targeted range-GET of T3_C1+T3_R1 canopy+confidence DEMs only; 2.28 MB transferred (2485x saving)
reference.frame: local-planar, no CRS, 0.01 m, ~10x1 m, origin ~(-5,0.5) — SAME convention as our pipeline DEM

key_findings: Published reference DEMs are ~FLAT: total tilt 0.91 deg (C1) / 1.32 deg (R1).
Our pipeline DEM is tilted 24.26 deg (long +11.92, cross +21.71) — reproduces day-2's 24.3 deg.
Long-axis: ref ~0 deg vs ours +11.9 deg. Cross-axis: ref <1.4 deg vs ours +21.7 deg. Neither grade is in the reference.
CLINCHER: our DETRENDED std (0.104 m) matches the reference RAW std (0.102 m C1 / 0.079 m R1) — same reef surface, rigidly rotated ~24 deg.
A 24 deg slope over a 10x1 m Keys patch-reef plot is implausible; ~1 deg (gently undulating) is realistic.
verdict: LEVELING ERROR — the ~24 deg tilt is a day-1 Step-11 frame-placement defect, NOT genuine reef slope.
implication: DEM/ortho are NOT product. Identity is already the flattest projection, so this CANNOT be fixed in the build; the fix is upstream (redo Step-11 leveling). Pilot SUCCEEDED: headless capability proven AND the defect was caught by the reference before shipping.
